correctness.rationale: For any nonadjacent set J of prescribed UD start positions, delete the disjoint blocks. Reinserting them at the designated slots in the original word is uniquely defined and preserves the height constraint, so there are exactly C_(n-|J|) realizations; adjacent prescribed starts are impossible. Expanding the product of the selected Walsh signs proves the formula on all 2n-1 coordinates. Put N=n+1. For j>=2, s2(N)<=s2(N-j)+s2(j)<=s2(N-j)+j-1. For odd n, N is even and s2(N-1)>=s2(N), which supplies the j=1 case. With v2(C_m)=s2(m+1)-1, every nonempty term is divisible by 2^s2(N), whereas the empty term has precisely one fewer factor of two. This includes n=1 and C_0. At even n the Narayana symmetry pairs peak counts of opposite parity; the full-support eigenvalue is zero. The orthogonal Walsh basis gives invertibility, determinant valuation and inverse-norm bound with the specified unnormalized kernel. The phrase 'zero-frequency counts' at lines 64–67 is to be read as counts of vanishing multipliers, not as the multiplier at the empty frequency.
residual_risks: The reproduction is finite. It does not establish complete even-order nullities or sharp real spectral gaps; the all-order claim rests on the proof.
